declared: 2026-10-06, before any live scenario was run
purpose: A controlled integration qualification: does a live authoritative game server carry the whole challenge path, from a secret-derived plan to verifiable evidence reproduced offline? Not a deployment, not a detection rate.

engine.name: Godot
engine.why: Unity and Unreal both need an account to download; Godot is MIT-licensed and downloads without one, runs a headless dedicated server on Linux, and its high-level multiplayer gives an authoritative server with stock clients in a few hundred lines.

subject: pilot-subject

scenarios.what: The subject plays normally: aims at and shoots the visible enemy, and never follows the probe.
The subject spins on the spot every few seconds, so the crosshair passes over the probe's direction briefly.
The server is told to place the probe where the subject has line of sight to it, breaking the placement rule; a responder then follows it.
The server is told to let the probe make footstep sounds the subject can hear; a responder follows it.
The server's audio query for the probe is switched off, so every sample reports audio unchecked; a responder follows it.
A deliberately broken emitter writes two events at the same moment that disagree about the probe's vision; a responder follows it.
The enemy stands in the open, in line with the probe behind the wall, and the subject aims at the visible enemy.
A server-side responder, standing in for a packet or memory reader, aims the subject at the probe it was sent: the behaviour such software produces, not cheat code.

checks: The plan is written by fpsdet challenge plan with a server-held secret; the server derives each realization from the secret and refuses a plan whose commitment its secret does not reproduce.
The probe is sent to the subject's client only, with the same fields as a real player, and the stock client receives it.
The stock client draws no pixel of the probe and plays no sound of it while the server reports vision and audio absent.
Every counted sample carries the server's own per-moment vision and audio verdict for the probe body.
Every case's packet and graph verify.
Scoring the captured telemetry twice, offline, gives the same decisions, observation ids, graph and packet as the live run's scoring.
After the match, the secret reproduces the plan, and the realization the server used.
No secret or realization value appears in any public output.

failures.expected: the server runs no challenge and says so; scoring without the plan reads no challenge sample
events naming an id no plan has are reported as unplanned and not read
a challenge planned for another player abstains as other_subject
the server refuses a plan for another match; events from another match are not read
samples outside the window are not read
a duplicated line adds nothing: one moment is one sample
a line with a channel state that is not known, absent or unchecked is rejected and reported
the realization cannot be reproduced and the tool says so; scoring and packet checks need no secret and still work
